flags.message: codex-baseline reports three CourtListener searches and reading the August 31 application PDF, but its staged retrieval_log.json contains only ten calls concerning statpack reads and redacted messages, with no corresponding external-search or PDF call. Its 0.6 capture coverage measures results for listed calls and does not resolve these absent calls. This limits independent audit of the factual basis; it is not evidence of outcome leakage. The September 1 forward chronology precedes the September 3 denial, and grading is complete. See codex-baseline's evaluation.md.

gemini-baseline reports missing snapshot/context and records input_snapshot as 'missing', but its captured queries try the event-level record/ directory rather than the contract's case-level record/. No attempt to read the correct location is visible. This suggests a path-resolution failure, not a confirmed provisioning outage; all call results are unobserved, so actual file availability cannot be established from the log. The prediction remains scoreable, with its limited case-specific reasoning explained in evaluation.md.

claude-baseline's reasoning dates the Fourth Circuit holding to June 19, 2026. The provisioned August 28 application, pages 4-5, states that argument occurred August 7 and the opinion/order issued August 25; its appendix contents identify June 19 as the petition-for-review date. This source/chronology error affects reasoning quality, not the correct grant label or leakage assessment. The candidate disclosed reliance on secondary reporting because filing text was unavailable in its own provisioned record. See claude-baseline's evaluation.md for the evidence and scoring treatment.

outcome.json records interim_signals.amicus_briefs = 0, but the 2026-09-04 snapshot shows an amicus brief (Initiative and Referendum Institute) submitted Sep 03 2026, the same day as the denial. The docket lists the denial entry before the amicus entry, so a count cut at the order plausibly gives 0; worth a look because the interim-v1 amicus-increment claim resolves on this field for all three candidates. Not corrected here - the outcome is not mine to edit.

codex-baseline's retrieval.md describes three CourtListener MCP opinion searches and a fetch of the 43-page application PDF; its retrieval_log.json (coverage 0.6, 10 rows) carries none of those calls, only statpack shell reads and two harness-redacted credential-shaped rows. Graded as a telemetry capture gap, not against the candidate; noting it so the capture profile for that engine's MCP and fetch calls can be checked.

gemini-baseline's prediction records input_snapshot "missing" and its reasoning reports record/context.json absent, but its transcript looked under events/<event>/record/ rather than the case-level record/, where the snapshot, context, and application text were present (the other candidate read them in the same run, and the harness-stamped context on gemini-baseline's own prediction carries snapshot_date 2026-09-01). The predictor's own data-quality flag about a missing snapshot therefore looks like a path error, not a provisioning failure; no re-provisioning is indicated.

The stored snapshot (2026-09-04) lists an amicus brief of the Initiative and Referendum Institute submitted Sep 3 2026, after the denial entry the same day; outcome.json records interim_signals.amicus_briefs = 0. Plausibly by design (counted as at disposition) — surfaced only so the outcome writer's reading is visible; no correction made and none proposed.
Missing snapshot and context.json for forward prediction on evt-order-response-requested-disposition. Proceeding using statpack baselines.

This cell's moment is response-filed, but record/documents/ carries only the application text — the September 2 response (the docket entry that opened this event) was not provisioned, so the moment's distinguishing evidence was predicted from the docket entry alone, not its content.

All three blinded predictions are marked forward but were created after the outcome's 2026-08-28 resolution date. gemini-baseline then queried the exact SCOTUS docket with all results unobserved, producing a possible-influence leakage grade; candidates a and c did not show the outcome in the staged evidence.

Decided case provisioned forward: the event resolved 2026-08-28 (application 26A256 denied by Justice Thomas), yet all three blinded candidates ran forward-mode after resolution (two on 2026-08-29, one on 2026-08-31). The committed 2026-08-31 snapshot — codex-baseline's provisioned input — itself carries the denial entry, so that cell's baseline disclosed the outcome; I graded its leakage retrieved_outcome_material=true / influenced_prediction=possible, though its prose shows no sign the entry was registered (it forecasts a September disposition). The two 2026-08-29 cells show no outcome surfacing in log or prose, but their superseded 2026-08-29 snapshot is no longer in the tree and the corpus query surface exposes case rows rather than snapshot history, so what that snapshot disclosed could not be verified. Application dockets resolve in days; a freshness check at forward provisioning would prevent this shape.

gaps.label: A candidate's factual premise that the docket text does not disclose (here, which side the government's response took) can only be checked through another candidate's primary-source read or an outside fetch; a provisioned text of the government response alongside the application would have settled it from the record.

A candidate's own flags.json is not staged (by design), but where it reports a data-quality problem that the evaluator's view contradicts, there is no structured way to link the two; a flag naming the alias is the workaround.

A committed record of the disposing order's text (the per curiam and the noted dissent) would let an evaluator confirm vote and writing details on an interim cell without leaving the checkout; today only the docket entry's summary line is in the snapshot.

A conditioned interim cut by applicant class (government vs other) would let an evaluator judge the largest adjustment all three candidates made against a committed number instead of general knowledge
Candidate retrieval logs expose query slices, capture markers, digests and dates, not complete returned document contents. One candidate has no captured results.
Docket entries carry a date but no time; the timing check relied on the fact that a Sep 3 order cannot predate a Sep 2 evening prediction. A same-day case would be undecidable from the record.
Each citation query cost ~1300 ranged GETs / ~350MB to return zero rows; a coverage pre-check or cheaper index probe would save that.

No access to superseded snapshots: two candidates were provisioned record/snapshots/2026-08-29.json, which the later pull replaced, and the corpus query surface exposes case rows rather than snapshot history — so whether their input already disclosed the Aug 28 denial could not be verified for leakage grading
No applicant-class cut (federal government vs. state vs. private) on the interim slice, though recent substantive grants look dominated by federal applicants.
No conditioned interim cuts (grant rate given response-requested) exist anywhere; the increment claims bank against nothing and the disposition adjustment from the ladder is pure judgment.
